clue.text: See 19
See 24
See doctor had rum

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the letters of these two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: An instruction to visit a physician who has been drinking rum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' looks like a verb telling you to visit; it is a noun, a bishop's diocese. Durham is a city in north-east England with an ancient bishopric.
explanation.definitionFit: A see is the district ruled by a bishop, and Durham is one of the oldest English bishoprics.

clue.text: Gives up before back-up guitar gets going

parts.note: to kick a habit is to give it up, so kicks means gives up

indicators.note: in a down clue, back-up means the word is read from the bottom upwards, so backwards

parts.note: a Strat is a Fender Stratocaster electric guitar

explanation.surface: A musician quits as soon as the backing guitarist starts to play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back-up' looks like a backing musician, but it tells you to read the guitar word upwards, giving TARTS.
explanation.definitionFit: To kick-start an engine or a project is to set it going with a sudden push.

clue.text: Return of service great up to this point

indicators.note: a return sends something back, so the letters of the following pieces are read in reverse

parts.note: the RAF (Royal Air Force) is one of the armed services
OS stands for outsize, meaning very large or great

explanation.surface: A tennis player's return of serve has been excellent so far.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Return of service' suggests tennis, but the service is the armed force RAF, and with OS it is read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: So far is the everyday idiom for until now, as far as things have gone.

clue.text: On the phone to purchase no-frills aircraft

indicators.note: on the phone we only hear words, so the indicator signals a soundalike

parts.note: to purchase is to buy, and something with no frills is plain

explanation.surface: Phoning to buy a basic budget plane.
explanation.definitionFit: A biplane is a type of aircraft with two pairs of wings, one above the other.

clue.text: Some milk to express? Nothing at all in emptied breast

indicators.note: in signals that the middle pieces are placed inside the letters left from the breast word
emptied removes all the inside letters of the breast word, leaving just its outside pair

parts.note: to utter something is to express it in words
FA is short for sweet FA, British slang for nothing at all

explanation.surface: A nursing mother finds she has nothing left to express from an empty breast.
explanation.walkthrough: Sweet FA is a British slang phrase for nothing whatsoever.
explanation.definitionFit: Butterfat is the fatty part of milk, so the clue's partitive phrase points to a component of it.

clue.text: Set puzzle ordinary solver easily finishes? Just the opposite

indicators.note: the opposite of finishes is starts, so the first letters of the next four words are taken

explanation.surface: A puzzle-setter claims an ordinary solver finishes easily, then admits the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finishes' first suggests last letters, which give nothing; 'Just the opposite' turns it to starts.
explanation.definitionFit: To pose a puzzle or question is to set it for someone to answer.

clue.text: Setter's dined in joiner's chipper

indicators.note: in places the setter and the eating pieces within the joining word

parts.note: and is a word that joins, a conjunction
the setter refers to themselves as I, so setter's is I'm
to dine is to eat, so dined is ate

explanation.surface: The puzzle-setter has eaten at a carpenter's cheerful dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joiner' looks like a carpenter, but it is the joining word AND.
explanation.definitionFit: Chipper is an informal word for cheerful and lively, which is what animated means.

clue.text: This paper briefly abandoned deadlines? They might be stoned

indicators.note: abandoned suggests wild, unrestrained, so the letters are rearranged
briefly cuts the last letter from the word paper

explanation.surface: A newspaper drops its deadlines, risking getting pelted with stones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deadlines' looks like newspaper time limits; read as dead lines it means words for the dead, carved on stone.
explanation.definitionFit: Epitaphs are inscriptions for the dead, often carved into gravestones, so they are lines about the dead set in stone.

clue.text: In short, I'm disgusted by most fruity type of language

indicators.note: in short means shortened, so the last letter is lopped off

parts.note: ugh is the exclamation of someone disgusted

indicators.note: most of a word means all but its last letter

parts.note: a fruity flavour or voice is rich

explanation.surface: Someone briefly expresses disgust at most of a fruity kind of language.
explanation.definitionFit: Ugric is a branch of the Finno-Ugric languages, including Hungarian.

clue.text: Agonised shout, if family fails to finish puzzle

indicators.note: an agonised shout is a contorted one, so the letters are twisted round
fails to finish means the last letter is not there

parts.note: kin means family

explanation.surface: A cry of anguish when relatives cannot complete a puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: Futoshiki is a Japanese logic puzzle based on inequalities in a number grid.

clue.text: Once again swallowed up British group, an aerospace one back in debt

indicators.note: in puts the band and the company inside the word for debt

parts.note: being in the red means being in debt, so red stands for debt

indicators.note: back means the band and company pieces are read in reverse

parts.note: Bros was a British pop group of the late 1980s
BAE Systems is a British aerospace group, one of the kind just named

explanation.surface: A financial report on a British aerospace firm being taken over again while in debt.
explanation.walkthrough: Bros was a British boy band; BAE Systems is a British aerospace company. In the red is the British idiom for overdrawn.
explanation.definitionFit: To reabsorb is to take in or soak up again, so the past tense means swallowed up once more.

clue.text: Puzzle only half completed by a footballer

indicators.note: only half the puzzle word is written, so its last three letters are dropped

parts.note: Kakuro is a Japanese number-crossword puzzle

explanation.surface: A footballer who has only got halfway through a puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: Kaka is the Brazilian footballer who won the Ballon d'Or in 2007.

clue.text: Pour out port down under, getting rollicking

indicators.note: out means the letters are put out of order
getting means the country takes in the port, so one goes inside the other

parts.note: down under is a nickname for Australia, abbreviated AUS
Rio de Janeiro is a famous port

explanation.surface: An Australian drinker gets merry pouring out the port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'port' looks like the wine; it is the harbour city Rio, placed inside AUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Uproarious and rollicking both describe noisy, boisterous fun.

clue.text: An interjection, perhaps by EEC?

definitions.meaning: an interjection such as oh or alas is one grammatical word class, an example of the category
the letters EEC sit inside the word speech, so they are a portion of it

explanation.definitionFit: Grammar names classes such as noun and interjection; the letters EEC are also literally a piece of the word speech.

clue.text: Nought for English in dish that's Thanksgiving grub

indicators.note: for signals that one piece replaces a letter, the E standing for English

parts.note: a tureen is a deep serving dish for soup
a duck is a score of nothing in cricket

explanation.surface: Swapping the English bit of a dish for nothing produces a Thanksgiving meal.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a batsman out without scoring is out for a duck. E is the abbreviation for English.
explanation.definitionFit: A turducken is a turkey stuffed with a duck stuffed with a chicken, an American festive roast.

clue.text: Trick discovered in puzzle

parts.note: a con is a trick or swindle
something discovered has been found

explanation.surface: A deception is uncovered within a puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: To confound someone is to baffle or perplex them, as a puzzle does.

clue.text: Book in store contains law that's easily bent

indicators.note: contains means the legal word sits inside the combined filing piece
in puts the book abbreviation inside the storage word

parts.note: to file papers is to store them
lex is the Latin word for law

explanation.surface: A book in a shop includes a law that is easy to get round.
explanation.definitionFit: Something flexible bends without breaking; a flexible rule is one easily bent too.

clue.text: Being completely wiped out by dodgy rite during sacrifice

indicators.note: during means the rearranged rite goes inside the offering word

parts.note: an oblation is an offering or sacrifice to a god

indicators.note: dodgy means unsound, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is annihilated in a botched sacrificial ritual.
explanation.definitionFit: Obliteration is total destruction, the state of being utterly erased.

clue.text: Surprisingly sulks, having liked our puzzles

indicators.note: surprisingly suggests something unexpected has happened to the letters, which are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone sulks despite liking this paper's puzzles.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram covers all the letters of 'sulks' and 'liked our'; 'having' just links them.
explanation.definitionFit: Killer sudokus are a harder variant of the sudoku number puzzle, adding cages with given sums.

clue.text: Megan's wrong about inner piece of jigsaw puzzle

indicators.note: about means the rearranged name goes round the chosen letter
wrong means the letters of the name are put in the wrong order

parts.note: the name Megan; the 's is just the verb is

indicators.note: inner piece of picks a single letter from inside the word jigsaw

explanation.surface: Megan has misplaced the centre piece of a jigsaw.
explanation.walkthrough: The letter taken from 'jigsaw' is its I, its second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An enigma is a mystery or riddle, something hard to work out.

clue.text: Friend has yen for sexually attractive American

parts.note: George Fox founded the Quakers, the Religious Society of Friends
Y is the abbreviation for the Japanese currency, the yen

explanation.surface: A friend falls for an attractive American.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has yen for' reads as fancying someone; really 'has' joins FOX and the yen symbol Y. A Friend is a Quaker, and Fox their founder.
explanation.definitionFit: Foxy is American slang for sexy, describing an alluring woman.

clue.text: Sinking of vessel Nemo managed without undue risk, largely

parts.note: sub is short for submarine, a vessel

indicators.note: managed means handled or worked over, so the letters are rearranged
largely means most of the word, so its last letter is dropped

explanation.surface: Captain Nemo's submarine dives without taking needless risks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without undue' only colours the surface; the fodder is NEMO and RIS. Captain Nemo commands the submarine Nautilus in Jules Verne.
explanation.definitionFit: Submersion is going under water, which is what a sinking vessel undergoes.

clue.text: Play in game, sat next to dealer

indicators.note: in means only what lies further inside the word game is kept, its closing pair, as though the play were concealed there
sat next to means the word dealer is placed against game, and only its opening letters run on from the join

explanation.surface: A card player sits beside the dealer during a game.
explanation.walkthrough: In effect the play is hidden across 'game' set next to 'dealer': the end of the first word and the start of the second, read across the join.
explanation.definitionFit: Medea is the tragedy by Euripides about the sorceress who kills her own children.

clue.text: Puzzle 14,225?

parts.note: the cross-reference to 14 across, whose answer is a grammatical class of word
225 is fifteen times fifteen, a square number

explanation.surface: A reference to a numbered puzzle, as though citing an old crossword.
explanation.walkthrough: The '14' is the cross-reference to 14 across; 225 is 15 squared, also the number of cells in this grid.
explanation.definitionFit: A word square is a puzzle grid whose words read the same across and down.

clue.text: Nude dancing entertains bar, that's clear

indicators.note: entertains means holds within, so the bar word goes inside
dancing means the letters move about into a new order

parts.note: to bar a way is to block it

explanation.surface: Naked dancing at a bar is declared acceptable.
explanation.definitionFit: Unblocked describes a pipe or way now clear of obstruction.

clue.text: Prison camp body regulating prisoners?

definitions.meaning: a German prisoner-of-war camp for captured officers in the Second World War
British regulators are named Of-something, like Ofwat for water; lag is slang for a convict

explanation.walkthrough: Ofwat, Ofgem and Ofcom are British watchdogs; one for lags would bear this name.
explanation.definitionFit: Oflag is short for Offizierslager, the German wartime camp for officer prisoners.

clue.text: Debtor desperately needs capital in eastern Germany

parts.note: DR is the accounting abbreviation for debtor

indicators.note: desperately suggests frantic disorder, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A debtor is in desperate need in an East German city.
explanation.definitionFit: Dresden is the capital city of Saxony, a state in eastern Germany.

clue.text: State (American) found in Chambers

indicators.note: found in means the American piece is located inside the chambers word

parts.note: the atria are the upper chambers of the heart

explanation.surface: An American state found listed in the Chambers dictionary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chambers' looks like the British dictionary, but here it is the heart's chambers.
explanation.definitionFit: Austria is a sovereign state, a country in central Europe.
